cases.text: Quantum decoherence occurs when a quantum system loses its state due to interaction with the surrounding environment. This process causes information stored in phase relations to leak into external environment, effectively collapsing the wavefunction into a classical probability distribution. To mitigate this effect, researchers employ error correction codes and isolation techniques to preserve fragile quantum states. A rigorous experimental framework must distinguish between intrinsic gate errors and environmental noise to accurately assess the fidelity and scalability of the underlying quantum calculations.
